title: Staged Terraform Compatibility Gates and Health Probe Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a staged compatibility and upgrade gating strategy for Terraform modules and providers used in Private (VPC) deployments. Define automated CI gates, in-cluster health probes, canary rollout steps, and a minimal version pin policy that enables safe rolling upgrades across customer VPCs without wideblast changes.
compatibility_matrix_sample: module/network v2.3.0 -> tested with terraform 1.5.9, aws provider 5.1.x (pin to 5.1.2), null provider 3.1.x
module/k8s-helm v1.4.1 -> tested with terraform 1.5.9, kubernetes provider 3.12.x (pin to 3.12.2), helm provider 2.8.x
module/storage v0.9.6 -> tested with terraform 1.4.0..1.5.9, google provider 4.70.x (pin to ~>4.70)
health_check_probes: Provisioning smoke: terraform apply in ephemeral environment must succeed within 12 minutes with no drift errors
Control-plane readiness: api-server healthcheck endpoint returns 200 within 2 minutes of k8s node join
KV cache benchmark: latencies under 4ms p50 for prefix-heavy workload (loadtest harness run)
Autoscaler sanity: dedicated pool scales from 1 to 5 nodes under synthetic 75% CPU for 60s without errors
ci_gate_rules: Pre-merge: tflint + tfsec + provider-compat lint (yaml manifest) must pass
Integration: terraform plan in canonical infra account, compare plan to known safe-diff whitelist; any unkown resource changes fail
Upgrade simulation: run 'terraform init -upgrade' in a clone workspace and run terratest suites for network, k8s, and storage modules
Policy as code: OPA/Rego policies deny changes that remove encryption, change KMS keys, or make S3 buckets public
Post-apply smoke: run remote-exec probes and report to rollout dashboard; failure marks rollout as failed and triggers rollback script
decisions: Adopt staged gates (dev -> staging -> canary -> prod) for module and provider upgrades rather than wide-pin freeze
Use selective pinning: pin provider minor.patch (e.g., 5.1.2) for modules that embed provider-specific behavior and use ~> semantics for stable providers
Enforce an automated ‘compatibility test run’ that confirms module+provider pairs against the canonical test matrix before any release
Rollouts will include a 24-hour canary window with elevated telemetry retention to detect regressions in latency and errors
tasks: Add a compatibility matrix YAML under infra/terraform/compatibility/compat-matrix.yml and populate initial entries
Implement CI workflow 'compat-check' that reads compat-matrix and runs terraform init -upgrade + terratest in gated runner
Create a canary overlay in the private-deployments repo that uses new provider pins and deploy to two non-production VPCs
Add health probes and custom alerts to the Console rollout dashboard for canary runs
Document rollback runbook and create a one-click rollback script in ops/playbooks/terraform-rollback.sh
acceptance_criteria: compat-matrix.yml contains entries for all modules referenced by private VPC terraform manifests
CI 'compat-check' job passes for at least two representative module upgrades in CI (network and k8s-helm)
Canary deployment runs and health probes report no regressions for 24 hours in telemetry dashboard
Runbook reviewed and signed off by Security and SRE (comments included below)
